messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Multiple QTL modelling in R/qtl2
messages.body_plain:
Hi there-- I'm trying to follow the conversation here but want to check my understanding-- PVE is percent variance explained? And the output from making that transformation is similar to comparing the variance of the phenotype residuals with and without a particular QTL-- because the same information goes into calculating the LOD score? Thanks for your time!

On Tuesday, August 27, 2019 at 9:53:07 AM UTC-5, Karl Broman wrote:

> Rather than use est_herit as your describe, I'd be more inclined to
> transform LOD scores.
> Provided you have no linked QTL, I'd compare the variance of the
> residuals with and without a particular QTL in the model, but I think
> this translates directly to the LOD score.
>
> I think ideally one would use the estimated coefficients under the
> fitted multiple-QTL model, but I'm not entirely sure how to do it.
>
> karl

messages.body_plain:
Might be an obvious question, but how should we treat QTL models with different generations of DO mice?
Must we specifically add them into the scan1() model as a covariate using addcovar/intcovar? Or are their differences controlled in some other portion of the qtl2 method, like in the HMM?

Thank you,

Excel

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] DO mice: ngen as a covariate
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] DO mice: ngen as a covariate
messages.body_plain:
You may or may not want to include generation cohort as an additive covariate in scan1(). It depends on whether there are systematic differences in phenotype between the generations, which is maybe often going to happen, but not universally.

Mostly, the generation number is used in the HMM to do the genotype reconstruction, as it affects the expected frequency of crossovers.

If you include generation cohort as a covariate, you'll need to make a numeric matrix with 0/1 indicator columns. If you include just generation number, it would assume that the trait is increasing/decreasing linearly with generation, which is probably not what you'd intend.

Perhaps something like this:

  X <- model.matrix(~ factor(mycross$covar$ngen) )[, -1]
  rownames(X) <- rownames(mycross$covar)

karl

messages.subject: Re: CC data in R/qtl2 format
messages.body_plain:
Karl,

Thank you for posting this data. I'm setting up an eQTL run for CC mice and would like to know if I'm using a valid approach.
My study design has 22 CC strains, all of which are represented in the Srivastava data, and 3 diets.

Assumptions that I made:

- cross$geno, cross$founder_geno, and cross$cross_info should be subset to my strains but otherwise unaltered.

- covariate matrix could be added with
>  > cross$covar <- covariateMatrix

- expression matrix could be added with
> > cross$pheno <- expressionMatrix

- the different diets could be represented in cross$pheno with a suffix
>  e.g CC001/Unc_Diet1; CC001/Unc_Diet2; CC001/Unc_Diet3

- cross$geno and cross$cross_info are the same regardless of diet, so we replicate the data for the same strains when adding in the different diet samples.

check_cross2 returns TRUE before adding in pseudomarkers using the following parameters: https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/blob/master/CC/R/calc_genoprob.R

I finished by using the modified cross2 to make gpr, apr, and kLOCO.

Appreciate your guidance as always,

Excel

On Tuesday, April 16, 2019 at 7:38:38 AM UTC-7, Karl Broman wrote:
> I've added some mouse Collaborative Cross genotype data in R/qtl2 format, at https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data.
> The data are taken from the supplemental data for Srivastava et al. (2017) Genetics 206:537-556, https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.116.198838
>
> There are still some problems. For example, CC037 is indicated in the Srivastava et al. (2017) supplemental data to have Y chromosome from the founder strain NOD, and to also have a large portion of the X chromosome from NOD. But the way R/qtl2 handles 8-way RIL, this should not happen.
>
> karl

Personally, I prefer not to answer questions of the form "is this a valid approach"?
I'm not comfortable serving as a rubber stamp for analyses when I'm not involved as a collaborator.

For the R/qtl2 list, I think it would be better to have more narrowly-focused questions, particularly regarding the software.

sorry,
karl

messages.subject_clean: fixed effects in a 4way via scan1coef
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl et al,
I am working with a 4-way mapping population where parental genotypes [A,B,C,D] come from two subspecies:
subspecies 1: [A,C]
subspecies 2: [B,D]

which produces four genotypes [AC,BC,AD,BD]:
fixed subspecies 1: [AC]
hybrids: [AD, BC]
fixed subspecies 2: [BD]

I want to use scan1coef to test three hypotheses with three separate contrasts:
H0 #1: parent A is the same as parent B, contrast = c(-1,1,-1,1)
H0 #2: parent C is the same as parent D, contrast = c(-1,-1,1,1)
H0 #3: subspecies 1 is the same as subspecies 2, contrast = c(-1,0,0,1)

So, I supply this contrast matrix to scan1coef:

```
contrast.mat <-cbind(
    mu = c(1, 1, 1, 1),
    add1 = c(-1, 1, -1, 1),
    add2 = c(-1, -1, 1, 1),
    fixed = c(-1, 0, 0, 1))
```

However, this matrix produces NAs for the fixed contrast. Is the issue the way that I am setting up the contrast matrix, or simply that I can't make this type of test simultaneously?

Any help is much appreciated.
Thanks,
John

Here is the code to replicate the issue:

```
data(fake.4way)
contrast.mat <-cbind(
  mu = c(1, 1, 1, 1),
  add1 = c(-1, 1, -1, 1),
  add2 = c(-1, -1, 1, 1),
  fixed = c(-1, 0, 0, 1))
sex.matrix <- as.matrix(fake.4way$pheno[,"sex"])
pheno.mat <- as.matrix(fake.4way$pheno[,"phenotype"])

probs <- qtl2convert::probs_qtl_to_qtl2(
  calc.genoprob(
    subset(fake.4way, chr = 1),
    step = 0))$probs
rownames(pheno.mat) <- rownames(sex.matrix) <- 1:nind(fake.4way)

s1coef.out <- scan1coef(
  genoprobs = probs,
  pheno = pheno.mat,
  kinship = NULL,
  addcovar = sex.matrix,
  intcovar = sex.matrix,
  se = TRUE,
  contrasts = contrast.mat)
```
